title: Low-degree derived cohomology map is epi
statement: Under the hypotheses of lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-truncation-iso, the induced map on degree j cohomology after right derivation is epi for every j ≤ n.

source.place: Lemma 05TC (lemma-negative-vanishing, line 5497), part (2) and its proof (lines 5525-5541): the triangle $\tau_{\leq a}K\to K\to\tau_{\geq a+1}K\to$, part (1) applied to its third vertex, and the long exact cohomology sequence; the statement above is that proof with the cone of $c$ in place of $\tau_{\geq n+1}K$

proof.text: Complete c to a distinguished triangle L → M → C → L[1] in D⁺(A). Map it to D(A) using the triangulated inclusion. For each i < n + 1, H^i(c) is an isomorphism, hence epic. The long exact sequence makes H^i(M) → H^i(C) zero. The map H^(i+1)(c) is monic by hiso if i + 1 ≤ n, and by hmono otherwise, since then i = n. Thus the connecting map is zero. Exactness at H^i(C), with both adjacent arrows zero, gives H^i(C) = 0. The cohomological characterization of the standard t-structure gives C.IsGE (n + 1). This is the proved private helper isGE_cone_of_homology_map.

Apply v.rightDerivedFunctorPlus and the triangulated inclusion into D(B) to obtain a distinguished triangle. Negative vanishing at the bound n + 1 gives zero cohomology of the derived cone in every degree less than n + 1.
For j ≤ n the derived cone has zero cohomology in degree j. Hence the map H^j(Rv M) → H^j(Rv C) is zero. Apply HomologySequence.epi_homologyMap_mor₁_iff to deduce that H^j(Rv c) is epic.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 05TC (lemma-negative-vanishing), proof of part (2), with the cone of c; the cone bound follows from the long exact cohomology sequence

lean.statement:
theorem epi_homologyFunctor_rightDerivedFunctorPlus_map
    {A : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} A] [Abelian A] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v₁} A]
    {B : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} B] [Abelian B] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v₂} B]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w₁} A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w₂} B]
    (v : A ⥤ B) [v.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits v]
    (n : ℤ) {L M : DerivedCategory.Plus A} (c : L ⟶ M)
    (hiso : ∀ i : ℤ, i ≤ n → IsIso ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor A i).map c))
    (hmono : Mono ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor A (n + 1)).map c)) :
    ∀ j : ℤ, j ≤ n →
      Epi ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor B j).map (v.rightDerivedFunctorPlus.map c))
